verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents a cross-session memory system: the agent writes durable plain-Markdown memory files to its workspace, and an active-memory feature performs rule-based memory recall that escalates to deep conversation-history recall when needed. This covers durable memory that is written and recalled. missing for 10: explicit documentation that memory writes happen automatically rather than only when the model chooses to save, depth on how recall is triggered without user prompting, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an everyday user, the assistant remembers me across sessions — durable long-term memory it can write to and recall from automatically

citations.quote: How OpenClaw remembers things across sessions

OpenClaw remembers things by writing plain Markdown files in your agent's
workspace (default `~/.openclaw/workspace`).
The model only remembers what gets saved to disk
Deep conversation-history recall that escalates only when rule-based memory recall is insufficient
